card.title: Opportunity for Influence
card.instruction: Find a path to greater influence in every assignment, setback, or unexpected responsibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put me on the broken printer? I'll need purchasing authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It just needs paper. There's a box by my desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll move it to mine and manage supplies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Then everyone will come to you when they run out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Have them bring their print jobs too, so I can decide which ones get priority.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 turns a printer job into purchasing authority, A3 turns paper fetching into supply management, and A5 converts demand handling into print priorities.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's simple paper solution gives A3 a resource to control; B4's acceptance of incoming requests gives A5 a decision point over work.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects the repair assumption and B4 names the real workload that comes with A's proposal.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's warning about everyone coming to A as a path to deciding which jobs matter.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish an apparently broken printer that only needs nearby paper.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's priority claim develops the specific resource access B4 has conceded.

coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; each reduced task becomes another route to influence.
